candidates.name: Knee Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: knees on the floor shorten the lever arm, a standard beginner regression that changes the resistance, not the pattern

candidates.notes: Standard entry regression for clients who cannot yet do a full push-up.

candidates.name: Pike Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: hips piked so the torso is near-vertical, shifting load from chest to the anterior deltoid in a shoulder-press vector

candidates.notes: Common bodyweight-only shoulder-press regression before handstand push-up work.

candidates.name: Elevated Pike Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: feet raised on a box steepens the torso further toward vertical, closer to a true handstand press line

candidates.notes: Bridges Pike Push-Up to Wall Handstand Push-Up.

candidates.name: Wall Handstand Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: fully inverted against a wall, true vertical overhead pressing line rather than a piked angle

candidates.notes: Wall-supported inverted press; the wall removes the balance failure mode of the freestanding version.

candidates.name: Freestanding Handstand Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: no wall support, so balance is a first-order failure mode of the rep, not just the setup

candidates.notes: Advanced skill; never auto-programmed per EL-5 (highest balance-failure risk of the handstand push-up line).

distinctFrom.why: hands turned out and torso leaned forward past the hands, loading the shoulder in a planche-lean vector instead of the flat horizontal press

candidates.name: Typewriter Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: stays in the bottom position and shifts weight side to side across a held rep, rather than pressing up-and-down onto alternating arms

candidates.notes: One-arm push-up progression tool; sustained bottom-position loading on one arm at a time.

candidates.name: Hindu Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: a flowing dive from downward-dog to upward-dog rather than a straight vertical press, adding a mobility component through the shoulders and thoracic spine

candidates.notes: Wrestling/yoga-derived flowing push variant; established staple of bodyweight programming.

distinctFrom.why: each rep drives a knee to the elbow, adding an oblique/hip-flexion demand on top of the press
one hand set forward of the other in a fixed offset rather than sweeping wide on each rep, a milder unilateral-bias step before the archer variant

candidates.name: Clap Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: explosive concentric leaves the floor for a clap, a plyometric/power expression rather than a controlled grind

candidates.notes: Plyometric, not cardio; never_auto per EL-5 (plyometric class).

candidates.name: Scapular Push-Up

distinctFrom.why: a new, small-range family: scapular protraction/retraction only, elbows locked, no elbow flexion at all

candidates.notes: Serratus anterior/scapular-control drill, quadruped or plank hold; classified under back per closed muscle vocabulary (no serratus entry).

candidates.name: Parallette Push-Up (Deep Range)

distinctFrom.why: parallettes give a fixed, stable elevated hand platform with a neutral wrist grip, versus stacked-plate/box deficits with a flat palm

candidates.notes: Parallettes only (rings variant is a suspension-family row); neutral-grip deep press.

distinctFrom.why: hands together on the same narrow overhand grip, not a shoulder-width neutral-grip attachment
body hangs to one side of the bar and alternates which shoulder clears it each rep, a rotational/unilateral-bias variant of the vertical pull
wide grip with one arm kept straight as a stabiliser while the other does the pulling work, an explicit one-arm-pull-up progression
legs held out in an L-sit for the whole set, adding a sustained hip-flexor/abdominal isometric to the pulling movement
one palm pronated and one supinated on the same rep, asymmetric forearm/bicep loading rather than a matched grip
starts at the top (jump or step up) and only performs the slow lowering phase, the standard beginner path to a first strict pull-up

candidates.name: Isometric Pull-Up Hold (Flexed Arm Hang)

distinctFrom.why: a held top-position isometric with no reps, a fixed-angle strength hold rather than a full concentric/eccentric cycle

candidates.notes: Time-based hold; exerciseType would be duration_hold rather than weight_reps.

distinctFrom.why: a small-range shoulder-depression drill from a dead hang, no elbow flexion, the movement a pull-up starts with
stays pulled to the top and traverses side to side across a held rep, rather than pulling up onto a straight-arm side each time

candidates.name: Muscle-Up (Bar)

distinctFrom.why: a pull-up immediately transitions into a dip over the bar in one continuous rep, combining two movement patterns

candidates.notes: Explicit never_auto per brief; high technical/timing complexity.

candidates.name: Weighted Chin-Up

distinctFrom.why: supinated grip biases the biceps and changes the loading vector, mirroring how Chin-Up is already a separate row from Pull-Up

candidates.notes: exerciseType would be weighted_bodyweight; loadSemantics ADDED_BODYWEIGHT (matches Weighted Pull-Up convention).

distinctFrom.why: torso leaned well forward and legs kicked back, shifting the emphasis from triceps to chest, the mirror of how upright-torso dips bias triceps
feet raised on a second bench increases the range and the proportion of bodyweight loaded through the arms
feet raised on a box brings the body closer to horizontal, increasing the proportion of bodyweight pulled
one arm pulls while the other stays free at the side, a unilateral loading vector the two-hand row cannot provide
a higher bar keeps the torso closer to vertical, a standard beginner-easy regression of the row angle
a low bar takes the body near horizontal, the hardest end of the row-angle range
supinated grip biases biceps more than the default overhand row, matching the Pull-Up/Chin-Up grip split already in the corpus
the non-working leg is held straight out in front rather than trailed back behind the body, a different balance and hamstring-flexibility demand

candidates.name: Assisted Pistol Squat (Chair-Assisted)

distinctFrom.why: a hand on a chair/rail removes most of the balance demand, the standard regression before the freestanding pistol

candidates.notes: gripDemand supportive (hand rests on a rail/chair for balance), not the grip-free freestanding pistol.

distinctFrom.why: the rear leg is held bent behind the body and the rear knee tracks toward the floor, removing the straight-leg counterbalance the pistol relies on
rear foot stays on the floor rather than elevated on a bench, the easier stationary-lunge entry point
unloaded bodyweight version of the existing dumbbell row, the implement (none vs dumbbell) is the distinguishing axis
the working leg steps forward under a lengthening quad rather than back, a different eccentric demand and knee-tracking profile
unloaded bodyweight version; implement axis (none vs dumbbell) makes this a separate row from the existing loaded one
unloaded bodyweight version; implement axis makes this a separate row from the existing loaded dumbbell one
unloaded bodyweight version; implement axis makes this a separate row from every loaded step-up already seeded
the step is to the side rather than straight ahead, adding a frontal-plane/adductor demand the forward step-up does not have
unloaded bodyweight version; implement axis makes this a separate row from the existing barbell one
legs switch mid-air between a lunge split stance each rep, rather than a symmetric two-leg jump
knees drive to the chest at the top of the jump, an explosive hip/knee-flexion expression rather than a squat-depth landing
one leg does the full bridge while the other is held off the floor, doubling the load on the working side, distinct from the shoulder-elevated Single Leg Hip Thrust
the top position is held while the legs alternate lifting off the floor, adding a pelvic-stability demand the static bridge does not test
the anti-flexion counterpart to the Plank/Hollow Body Hold family; loads the posterior chain isometrically face-down rather than the anterior core
performed on all fours moving an opposite arm and leg rather than lying on the back moving limbs against gravity
a short maximal-tension protocol (glutes, quads and lats actively squeezed) prescribed for far shorter holds than the standard endurance plank
forearms are walked forward past the shoulders, lengthening the moment arm and increasing anti-extension demand for the same body position
a repeated dip-and-raise of the hip rather than a static hold, a rep-based rather than isometric prescription of the same position
small continuous alternating up-down kicks with the legs held low, not a full raise to a fixed top position
legs cross over each other horizontally rather than moving up and down, adding an adductor crossover component
one hand lifts to tap the opposite shoulder each rep, adding an anti-rotation demand the static plank does not require
alternates between forearm plank and full push-up plank each rep, adding a repeated pressing transition to the static hold
legs are raised then swept side to side under control while hanging, a rotational demand a straight vertical toes-to-bar does not test
performed hanging from a bar with a closed grip, not supported on parallettes/the floor with palms pressing down
legs are raised well above parallel into a V rather than held level with the hips, a harder end of the same range-of-motion progression
bridges forward onto the forehead loading neck flexors, the mirror of the existing back-of-head extensor bridge
a static inverted hold against a wall; distinct from the pressing-rep Wall Handstand Push-Up
no wall support; balance is the entire challenge rather than a setup convenience
entry point of the planche progression: a plank-position hold with the torso leaned forward past the hands, feet still on the floor
feet leave the floor entirely with knees tucked to the chest, a full support hold rather than a leaning drill
a horizontal straight-body hold hanging from a bar, mechanically distinct from any vertical pulling row already seeded
legs fully extended straight out rather than tucked, a much longer lever arm on the same hold
body hangs face-down and behind the bar in a false grip rather than face-up in front of it, a straight-arm shoulder-extension hold instead of a pulling hold
a horizontal side-on hold gripping a vertical pole with both hands, a lateral-flexion/anti-rotation demand no other seeded row provides
knees are tucked toward the chest rather than legs extended straight, shortening the lever arm as the standard entry progression

rejected.name: Nordic Curl (Eccentric-Only, Assisted)
rejected.reason: not distinct under EL-2 (a coaching cue/assistance level on the existing Nordic Curl, not a new movement)

rejected.name: Single-Leg Box Jump
rejected.reason: not representable (box-height-dependent, not a fixed taxonomy point; belongs to a curated plyometric style pool, not a generic library row)
